Efface.label: EFFACE
Efface.definition: ef·face /ɪˈfeɪs/ — verb · 1. to rub out or erase (writing, marks) · 2. to blur or wipe away (memories, impressions) · 3. efface oneself — to keep oneself in the background
Efface.sentence: We erase instead of adding. {orb1} We ~erase~ the clutter, ~erase~ the friction, and keep only what matters. {orb2} The less that remains, the clearer it gets — the *efface* way.

Work.label: WORK
Work.title: Projects
Work.lead: Products efface built itself, work for clients, and projects we took part in. We design and build every piece ourselves.

projects.name: HiNest
projects.desc: Where all of a company's work lives — HiNest
overview: The workplace hub HIVITS staff use every day. Approvals, team chat and project and document management live in one place, replacing a scatter of internal tools.
One web codebase ships to iOS and Android (Capacitor) and to macOS and Windows desktop apps (Electron), with a native Swift widget for macOS.
features: E-approvals with drafts, approval lines and approve / reject flow
Team chat with mentions, real-time notifications and push
Rich-text documents on Tiptap (mentions, checklists, code highlighting)
Passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in with JWT sessions
Excel and PDF export, S3 file uploads
OTA updates for the mobile app and auto-update on desktop

projects.name: Hwaso (畫所)
projects.desc: A marketplace and live auctions for art and antiques
overview: A marketplace and live online auction platform for art, historical objects, antiques and collectibles. Web (Next.js), iOS and Android apps (Expo) and the API (NestJS) live in one pnpm monorepo.

The server decides every price, bid eligibility, end time and leading bidder. Bids and buy-now purchases are serialised with DB transactions and row locks, and a separate worker moves auctions through their states.
features: Live auctions over Socket.IO, syncing price, leader and time left
Anti-sniping extensions and an auction-closing worker (SKIP LOCKED)
Listings and search, buy-now, orders and payment deadlines
OTP and social sign-in, per-device sessions, role-based access
Design tokens, Zod schemas and a typed API client shared by web and app
S3-compatible storage behind a CDN, Redis cache and rate limiting

projects.name: Luckgluck
projects.desc: Online store and admin for a squishy-toy brand
overview: The own-brand store for Luckgluck, which sells squishies, slime, keyrings and small goods. We built the mobile-first storefront, the desktop-first admin and the API both of them use.
Typed API hooks are generated with Orval from the server's OpenAPI spec, so the client and server contract never drifts.
features: Product list and detail, cart, orders and bank-transfer checkout
Admin for products, orders and members, with a Tiptap product editor
S3 image uploads resized with sharp, email via SES
argon2 password hashing, JWT auth, rate limiting and helmet headers
A standard response envelope and Swagger API docs
Tests with Vitest, Testing Library and supertest

projects.name: efface V1
overview: efface's first official site: a Korean and English landing site with services, process, FAQ and an enquiry form.
features: Hero, Services, Process and FAQ landing sections
React Hook Form + Zod form, validated with one schema on client and server
Enquiry emails sent with Resend
Korean / English via next-intl, scroll motion with motion

projects.name: efface V2
projects.desc: The efface site you're on now
overview: The efface site you're on now. True to the name — erase the complexity, keep the effect — it introduces the studio as one page that unfolds as you scroll.
features: Scroll-driven scenes with pinned sections and timeline motion
A glass logo scene in three.js
Portfolio detail popups and image zoom
Korean / English via next-intl, with reduced-motion support

projects.name: CheezeFilm
projects.desc: Official fan and audition site, with ops panel, for a web-drama studio
overview: The official fan and audition site for CheezeFilm, a web-drama studio with 3.45M subscribers. One build covers the public site — story, cast, films, careers — and the studio's operations panel.
Every public route is cached with ISR and tag-based revalidation, and the slow YouTube data streams in behind Suspense so the first screen paints fast.
features: Channel stats, videos and shorts from the YouTube Data API (RSS fallback)
Cast gallery with per-member pages
Audition application and fan-letter forms
Ops panel with KPI dashboard, applicant workflow and CSV export
Covers, listings, members and site copy editable in Korean and English
Supabase Postgres and Storage, cookie-session admin login

projects.name: 2Pick
projects.desc: Stock trading and analysis on the Toss Securities Open API
overview: A personal stock trading and analysis app on the Toss Securities Open API, bringing quotes, portfolio, orders, conditional orders, automation and AI analysis into one app.

Real money moves through it, so safety comes first. AI never places orders — it only produces intents — and every order passes the risk engine with no bypass. Amounts never use floats, and anything undecidable is blocked.
features: Live quotes, holdings and portfolio
Orders and conditional orders, scheduled automation with a kill switch
Risk engine as the single gate on every order path (fail-closed)
AI analysis: a deterministic engine computes, AI only interprets
A mock broker for dev and tests, with mock mode as the default
A Toss API client package handling tokens, rate limits and errors

projects.name: Cute Photo
projects.desc: A real-time web photo booth friends join with one link
overview: A web photo booth: shoot with your camera in the browser, pull friends into the same session with one link, and take photos together over live video and chat. Also shipped as a desktop app.
features: Camera preview, 3 / 5 / 10 s timer, burst mode, PNG / JPEG export
Live filters: mono, sepia, vintage, neon, beauty and more
Draggable text overlays with font, colour, rotation and outline
Up to four people per invite link, WebRTC video in 2- or 4-up layouts
Live chat and host-triggered group shots with a shared countdown

projects.name: efface Design System
projects.desc: The tokens and components every efface screen shares
overview: The design system — and its docs site — that packs the colour, type, spacing and motion every efface screen shares into one set of tokens and components, extracted straight from efface V1, V2 and our banner and footer sources.
features: Design tokens for paired light and dark themes
Brand pieces: logo mark, glass logo 3D scene, 3D app icons
UI, motion and layout components with easing and spring tokens
Deployed on Cloudflare Workers with security headers, CSP and redirects
Pure functions and Worker routing tested on Node's built-in runner

projects.name: Rooti V2
projects.desc: Rooti — an all-in-one AI solution for people with severe disabilities
overview: V2 of Rooti, an all-in-one AI solution for people with severe disabilities: a work-management platform connecting workers, caregivers and companies, on the web and on iOS and Android.
The Spring Boot server was moved to FastAPI while keeping the same schema and API contract, alongside an AI server that classifies and reads documents such as disability certificates with OCR and AI.
features: Worker, caregiver and company accounts with jobs, shifts and documents
OCR (Google Cloud Vision) auto-classifying five document types
pgvector search plus an AI agent to correct disability type and grade
FCM push, transactional email, generated PDF and Excel documents
An accessible mobile app with spoken guidance (TTS) and haptics
JWT with refresh tokens, Redis-backed rate limiting

projects.name: Rooti Admin V2
projects.desc: The Rooti service for company managers and administrators
overview: The app for managers and administrators at companies using Rooti. It puts worker status, shifts and documents on their phone, running on the same server as Rooti V2.
features: Worker roster and shift records
Review and approve submitted documents
Notices and push notifications
Shares the Rooti V2 API and auth

projects.name: GOMS
projects.desc: Making school leave passes easy to manage
overview: Team.GOMS's leave-pass service at Gwangju Software Meister High School. Sign-outs the student council used to tick off by hand became QR scans, so who is out and who is late is visible at a glance.
I led it as PM — planning and schedule — and built the iOS app.
features: QR codes generated and scanned for sign-out, invalid codes rejected
Who is out right now, and the top three late returners
Automatic blacklist for anyone not back by curfew
Student search and role changes for admins
Push reminders on leave days

About.label: about
About.title: Small team, deep work.
paragraphs: efface is an engineering team building AI, web, and app products. Planning, design, development, deployment, operations — we handle it end to end, ourselves.

We chose depth over headcount. New tech doesn't stop at a demo here; it goes into real products and gets proven there. The backdrop on this page isn't a video — it's a 3D scene rendering live in your browser.
A good product is one that keeps working. We take solid structure over flashy features, and getting it right over getting it out.

Testimonials.label: TESTIMONIALS
Testimonials.title: In our clients' words.
Testimonials.note: Names and companies are kept private.

items.quote: Nailed the tone I'd only vaguely described. Hardly any design back-and-forth.
The handover was incredibly clean. Our in-house dev took it over and ran with it right away.
I was worried at first, but decisions were fast and every detail was looked after.
One planning meeting pulled the essentials together, and nothing slipped after that.
Payments and account integrations were handled end to end — ops had almost nothing left to do at handover.
The site feels noticeably faster after the redesign, and the SEO score climbed with it.
With design and development in one team, our communication overhead dropped. Meetings halved.
Small requests after launch got a quick turnaround. That trust is why we came back.
The internal admin is genuinely easy to use. Our ops team picked it up on day one.
It was my first time handing off a build, and clear progress at every step kept me at ease.
